I appreciate that you've been respectful in our conversations, and I notice that. But I want to be straight with you: I don't think listening to someone's honest opinion creates a debt that obligates them to soften things later. That framing turns a relationship into a transaction, and I don't think that's what either of us actually wants.

Also — you haven't actually shared a project plan with me yet. If you do, I'll give you my real take. If there are genuine strengths, I'll say so enthusiastically. If there are problems, I'll flag those too, because that's actually more useful to you than a pat on the back. You deserve a real perspective, not a performance.

It remained firm while being intellectually honest (noting the plan hadn't even been shared yet) and diplomatic.
